title: Novelty in Content Creation: Experimental Results Using Deep Learning-Based Image Recognition on a Large Social Network
eligible_reason: Staggered binary treatment within a field experiment on Behance: 329 randomly selected artists were 'featured' at user-specific dates (79 distinct hashed feature_date values among treated users; code comments place the experiment between 2015-08-03 and 2015-10-21), 329 control artists were never featured. Every main regression is a static TWFE on project-level observations: felm(outcome ~ treatment_x_post_feature | user_id + week_id | 0 | user_id) with no controls and no weights (lfe). Units are users (stable), time is the hashed calendar week of project creation (repeated cross-section of projects assigned to users). At least two cohorts, never-treated controls present, no time-varying controls.
design_notes: mainData.csv: 4,487 projects by 658 users (329 treated / 329 control), 40 distinct hashed week_id values, each project one row; the featured project itself is excluded from all regressions. treatment_x_post_feature = 1 for the 1,386 treated-user projects created after the feature date, 0 for the 1,044 treated-user pre-feature projects and all 2,057 control projects; 252 treated users have both pre and post projects. Feature dates differ across treated users (79 distinct hashes), i.e. staggered adoption at the daily level; at the weekly level the number of cohorts is smaller (the experiment spans about 11-12 weeks). IMPORTANT for CSA/BJS: week_id and feature_date are hashed, so calendar ordering of periods is not directly available; a partial ordering can be reconstructed from within-user pre/post patterns (for every treated user, all weeks with post==0 precede all weeks with post==1; 9 treated users have the same week both pre and post, pinning their feature week), but exact timing is withheld by the authors ('Code but not data are provided ... for additional analyses which require individually identifiable data such as exact feature timing'). All variables are 'fuzzed', so package estimates differ slightly from the published ones and SEs are inflated (README). Two-months-post interaction (lines 225-227) adds a second treatment regressor (ineligible). Image-level data and created_timestamp (needed for lines 143-153, 159-222) are not shipped. SUTVA check (folder 5) is t-tests only; external validation (folder 3) is logit/OLS on survey data.
n_eligible_specs_note: 71 static TWFE specs replicable from mainData.csv (7 label outcomes, 9 distance outcomes, 4 keyword outcomes, 36 above/below-median sample splits, 12 alternative-centroid novelty measures, 3 no-training-image measures). Which of these appear in the main text vs. the online appendix cannot be determined without the article. 19 further qualifying specs need unshipped data (image-level file, created_timestamp); 3 specs with the two-months interaction are ineligible.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: 79 distinct hashed feature_date values among the 329 treated users (daily granularity); fewer distinct weeks. Control users have feature_date = NA.
reports_modern_estimator_note: No CSA/SA/BJS/dCDH code in the package; the full-text flags (Callaway, de Chaisemartin) suggest the paper cites them in discussion. Re-check against the article.
preferred_spec_note: Guess: the paper's novelty measure is the distance between new projects and the featured project in the 7-dimension label embedding; the code runs these first after the label regressions. Unverified without the article.

data_access_detail: fuzzed real data: README states identifiers are hashed and 'variables have been fuzzed to protect the privacy of study participants, causing results to differ slightly and standard errors to be inflated'; user-level network features and exact feature timing removed. Treated as disguised per protocol instruction.
data_files: Replication Package/Replication_Folders/4. Main Analysis/mainData.csv (3.3 MB, 4,487 rows, 45 columns; csv)
data_files_note: mainData.csv contains every variable used by the eligible specs (outcomes, treatment_x_post_feature, user_id, week_id, above_median, featured_project_id). Not shipped: imageLevelData, created_timestamp, unhashed week/feature dates.
software_notes: R 4.3.1, dplyr + lfe::felm (mainAnalysis.R); Stata for word embeddings (folder 2); Python/TensorFlow for image classification (folder 1).
replication_feasible_note: TWFE is directly replicable on the fuzzed data (FE need no time ordering). CSA/BJS require ordering weeks and assigning cohorts: feasible only if the week order can be reconstructed from the pre/post pattern (partial order over 40 weeks from 252 treated users) or if the authors supply the week/feature-date mapping.
priority_note: Eligible design with data in the package, but data are fuzzed and time ordering is hashed; main-text table assignment unknown.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Treatment timing checked in mainData.csv (python): 79 distinct feature_date among treated, NA for all controls; treatment_x_post_feature is 0 for all control rows. Sample splits by above_median are eligible as sample restrictions; lines 68-69 cluster by project_id (apparent typo). Year 2025 taken from the batch file (OpenAlex frame lists the abstract only).
